findings.label: Original z-score dip/up scanner
findings.detail: 0/32 basket x direction cells significant at 2-year or 7-year lookback across the full 104-ticker universe.

findings.label: Cross-sectional momentum (12-1 month)
findings.detail: The row-level result disappeared after block bootstrap accounted for cross-sectional and serial dependence.

findings.label: Relative, breakout, PEAD, fundamentals, and analyst-rating signals
findings.detail: No tested direction survived confirmation-only, dependence-aware significance testing.

findings.label: Analyst price-target consensus gap
findings.detail: 0/2 confirmation-period primary cells significant. The 'dip' leg fired on ~69 tickers/day on average (structural optimism bias in sell-side targets); the 'up' leg showed a discovery-to-confirmation sign flip.

findings.label: Cross-asset macro signals (VIX spike, credit spread, yield curve)
findings.detail: 0/2 confirmation-period primary cells significant for all three signals under same_close (unrealistic) entry timing. Credit spread's 'up' leg looked strongly significant in discovery (p<0.001) but flipped to a small non-significant edge in confirmation. Re-checked 2026-07-26 under realistic next_open entry timing: VIX and yield curve unchanged (still rejected); credit spread's DIP leg flipped from non-significant (p=0.128) to significant (p=0.0, mean edge +1.39%) in confirmation. NOT elevated to confirmed/promising -- testing both timings without pre-registering which one counts is an uncorrected extra look (same multiple-testing risk this project's own by-block docstring warns about for weighting/block-length variants). Treat as an unconfirmed anomaly pending a dedicated, properly-scoped re-test (block-length sensitivity, trade_weighted comparison, and ideally a fresh discovery/confirmation split with next_open pre-registered as the only timing tested) before trusting it.

findings.label: Momentum (12-1 month) and analyst price-target gap under realistic next_open timing
findings.detail: Re-checked 2026-07-26 under next_open entry timing (previously only tested under same_close): both remain 0/2 confirmation-period primary cells significant, materially unchanged from the same_close result. Closes the entry-price look-ahead gap from memory:project_execution_realism_gaps for these two signals.

findings.label: QQQ/TQQQ trend+volatility regime rotation
findings.claim: Beats 50/50 buy-and-hold on both CAGR and drawdown
findings.detail: The apparent result depended on a corrected same-close look-ahead bug and did not survive the main confirmation on CAGR.

findings.label: SOXX/SOXL trend+volatility regime rotation — return
findings.detail: The pre-tax return advantage disappeared after the modeled short-term capital-gains tax.

findings.label: SOXX/SOXL trend+volatility regime rotation — drawdown
findings.detail: Maximum drawdown remained materially lower across confirmation, walk-forward, sensitivity, and tax/cost checks. This is a risk result, not a confirmed excess-return result.

findings.label: Kelly-criterion sizing with one-way profit ratchet
findings.claim: Improves risk-adjusted return over plain inverse-volatility targeting
findings.detail: Looked like a breakthrough on a single discovery/confirmation split but failed walk-forward validation. Structural flaw: the one-way ratchet can never re-lever once trimmed, so it structurally misses upside in an extended bull market. Kelly sizing itself (signed mean/variance) is a genuine improvement over inverse-vol targeting; the ratchet is the part that broke.

findings.label: Wide rebalance band vs. tight/continuous vol-targeting
findings.claim: Reduces tax/turnover cost without giving up performance
findings.detail: ~89% less tax/turnover for essentially the same performance as continuous vol-targeting.

findings.label: Volatility-targeted leveraged-ETF rotation — 3-pair validation
findings.claim: The vol-targeting rotation mechanism generalizes beyond SOXX/SOXL
findings.detail: Same continuous inverse-vol-targeted weighting tested on SPY/UPRO and NVDA/NVDL in addition to SOXX/SOXL, at the user's request, as production candidates. Backtested/designed only -- not yet in live/paper trading.
